"**CO 1 ////// -- 1 Congenital Talipes Equinovarus CTEV / Clubfoot**

**Introduction**
**Definition** CTEV is a complex congenital deformity of the foot characterized by four distinct components Equinus plantarflexion at the ankle Varus inversion of the subtalar joint Adduction of the forefoot and Cavus exaggerated medial longitudinal arch It is commonly remembered by the mnemonic CAVE
**Clinical Features** The foot is turned downwards and inwards resembling a club Deep creases are visible on the medial border and posterior aspect of the heel The heel is small and empty calcaneus is pulled up The calf muscles especially on the affected side are visibly atrophied and underdeveloped It is a rigid deformity that cannot be passively corrected to a neutral position Can be unilateral or bilateral
**Investigations** Clinical Diagnosis Diagnosis is primarily clinical immediately at birth X rays AP and Lateral views of the foot in stress dorsiflexion Used to assess the severity and document the baseline bony alignment Kites angle talocalcaneal angle X rays are also used to monitor the progress of correction
**Complications** If untreated the child walks on the dorsolateral aspect of the foot Formation of painful large callosities and bursa over the weight bearing area Awkward limping gait Rocker bottom foot iatrogenic complication if the midfoot is forced into dorsiflexion before the heel equinus is corrected Severe psychological and cosmetic impact
**Medical / Conservative Management** Ponseti Method Gold Standard Serial manipulation and casting starting within the first week of life The deformities are corrected in a specific order Cavus Adductus Varus and finally Equinus Casts are changed weekly Splinting After full correction the foot is maintained in a Denis Browne splint or Foot Abduction Brace full time for 3 months then at night until 4 years of age to prevent relapse
